transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-04
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~50 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Claire (CTO, Seabreeze), Tom (Dir Infra), Sofia (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be partial):
- Seabreeze interested in renewing current contract and expanding capacity into EU region; exploring Dedicated capacity vs hosted with VPC; wants pricing for 12-month extension with additional reserved GPUs and region add-on.
- Security: SOC 2, KMS, audit logs required; legal/procurement timeline ~2 weeks.
- Action items: Redwood to send pricing/contract amendment, run EU benchmark, Seabreeze to share QPS windows.

Topics: renewal, dedicated capacity, EU region, VPC/private deployment, contract term, security/compliance

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we wanted to run through the renewal and expansion asks for Seabreeze. I know we have a few items on the agenda - capacity for holiday, adding EU region, and contract term. Claire, do you want to kick us off with where you are on internal timeline?

[00:22] Claire: Yeah thanks Maya. We're targeting to have procurement signed by mid-November if possible, so we have the capacity prepped for the Thanksgiving Black Friday window. So timeline is tight. Also we'd like to expand into EU because about 30% of our customers are EU and latency right now is a bit rough.

[00:40] Tom: Just to add, our current pattern is spiky; peak QPS is about 1.8k for recommendation endpoint and we see bursts up to 3k sustained for 45-90 minutes during promos. We want to make sure whatever we pick can handle short bursts without big fallback failures.

[01:05] Ethan: Got it. For context, based on the numbers you just said, dedicated reserved GPU capacity gives the most predictable throughput and avoids noisy neighbors during the peaks. We can model an autoscale/burst setup with a base reserved pool plus burst to shared capacity - that usually hits the SLOs without overprovisioning.

[01:30] Claire: Okay but cost is a concern. We want to see the delta between hosted with higher limits vs a Dedicated small cluster, and the quantization options you recommended previously.

[01:50] Maya: Totally. We'll send a pricing comparison. Quick note - our "Redwood Dedicated" pools are the reserved option, but I sometimes hear it called Redwood Dedicate in notes - sorry if that shows up in any docs.

[02:03] Sofia: On procurement side, we need the redlined SOW and SOC 2 docs. Also can you confirm if KMS integration is supported for EU regions? Our security team insists on customer-managed keys.

[02:20] Ethan: Yes, we do support KMS/HSM integrations. For hosted EU regions we can integrate with the customer's KMS in most cases, but for Private/VPC it's more straightforward. I'll put a note to include the exact KMS playbook and limitations - sometimes there's a slight delay for cross-region key replication.

[02:45] Tom: What about data residency? We need to ensure no customer PII leaves the EU for EU tenants.

[02:52] Maya: For the EU add-on we can provision region-specific endpoints and ensure data at rest in EU. If you need a Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) we can do that too but that's usually a separate licensing and timeline.

[03:10] Claire: Timeline for Private is longer though right? For holiday we probably can't do Private. So leaning Dedicated in EU or hosted with EU endpoints.

[03:22] Ethan: Correct - private deployments typically take 6-10 weeks depending on networking and KMS setup. Dedicated EU capacity can be live in 1-2 weeks once we agree on size and contract.

[03:38] Claire: That fits better. Can you give a ballpark cost for the dedicated pool sized for our estimated peaks?

[03:45] Maya: We'll have that in the pricing doc, but high-level estimate - based on the 3k bursts and 1.8k baseline, a dedicated pool with N GPUs (we'll propose specific instance types) plus a small shared burst allowance should be 20-30% cheaper than trying to overcommit on hosted per-token pricing during the season. We'll send concrete numbers.

[04:10] Tom: For the benchmark, can Redwood run a synthetic load test from EU to confirm p99 latency at our peak QPS?

[04:18] Ethan: Absolutely. I'll run an EU-dedicated sizing benchmark and include p50/p90/p99 latency curves and token throughput. We'll also test with quantized models vs 8-bit to show cost/latency tradeoffs.

[04:35] Claire: Great. Also, are there any fallbacks if the dedicated pool is exhausted? We can't have user-facing errors.

[04:42] Ethan: We recommend automated smart routing: fallback to a compatible hosted model in another region or lower-cost variant. We can set route policies by latency tolerance; we can also configure a circuit-breaker so requests queue for X seconds before hitting fallback, to avoid error spikes.

[04:58] Sofia: Legal question - if we extend for 12 months with a capacity add-on, are there discounts for committed spend?

[05:04] Maya: Yes, reserved capacity monthly/annual commits come with tiered discounts. For a 12-month extension and reserved blocks we'll put together tiered pricing in the SMA/contract amendment.

[05:18] Claire: Competitors - we've looked at Bedrock and Anthropic pricing, part of our assessment is unit economics and latency. Any benchmarking you can share comparing to those would help.

[05:28] Maya: We have internal perf sheets and some public benchmarks; I can share a sanitized spreadsheet that compares p99 latency and token cost across model families. Fair warning the numbers vary a lot by prompt shape.

[05:42] Tom: Also we need traceability/audit logs for API usage per team. Our compliance wants token-level logging where possible.

[05:50] Ethan: We provide per-route usage logs and tracing hooks in Redwood Console; audit logs can be exported to S3 or a customer-managed log sink. We also support role-based access control (RBAC) across teams.

[06:05] Claire: That should satisfy SOC 2. One more thing - how do we handle rollouts? We want canary first for the new region.

[06:12] Ethan: Canary and A/B rollouts are standard. We can provision a canary subset in EU and route 5-10% traffic for the first 24-48 hours and monitor quality/regressions. If we see score drops we can auto-fallback.

[06:25] Maya: Okay quick recap on what we need to deliver: pricing + contract amendment, EU sizing benchmark, SOC2/KMS docs, and we'll schedule a VPC/private demo if needed.

[06:34] Claire: Yes. Also can you include an appendix showing the expected cost delta for quantized models? Our ML team is open to 8-bit if latency tradeoff is acceptable.

[06:43] Ethan: I will include quantization profiles and recommended models per workload. We'll show accuracy deltas vs cost.

[06:52] Tom: If we do the EU dedicated pool, what's the failover plan to US region? Will we cross-backhaul traffic?

[06:59] Ethan: Failover to US is possible but not recommended for EU-residency sensitive customers. For redundancy we can provision multi-AZ in EU and a secondary hot standby in EU region. Cross-region failover is optional and can be controlled by policy.

[07:15] Sofia: Procurement timeline - we'll aim to review the contract within 3 business days of receiving the amendment. If we can get the doc by Monday we should be good.

[07:23] Maya: We'll aim to send the amendment and pricing today or tomorrow.

[07:30] Claire: One small note - our security team asked about private networking egress costs; do you have guidance?

[07:36] Ethan: Egress is standard cloud egress and depends on region; we'll include estimated network egress in the cost appendix. For Private deployments egress is managed by your infra.

[07:48] Speaker 1 (automated): [unintelligible, overlap]

[07:52] Maya: okay I think that's most of the big stuff. Next steps recap: Maya sends contract and pricing, Ethan runs EU benchmark, Claire sends peak QPS and holiday windows, Sofia confirms procurement dates, schedule a follow-up check in next week.

[08:10] Claire: Thanks - one last question, do you support per-customer isolation at the model level? For some regions we want tenant-specific models.

[08:20] Ethan: We do. You can pin model versions per tenant and run canaries per-tenant; dedicated pools can be partitioned logically or physically. We'll include a short note in the doc.

[08:33] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in writing and set the calendar for the sizing deep dive. Appreciate your time.

[08:40] Meeting end.

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mis-attribution and auto-caption artifacts; product names may be slightly off ("Redwood Dedicate", "Redwood Privet"), numbers transcribed approximately.
